title: Securities Trading Policy

tiers.name: Applicable Persons
tiers.description: Directors, employees, advisers, contractors and consultants of WAF. Bound by the insider trading prohibition and encouraged to counsel their Related Persons, but not subject to Closed Periods, notification, the short-term trading ban, the derivatives criteria or the margin lending rules, which are all confined to Key Management Personnel.

tiers.name: Key Management Personnel
tiers.description: As defined in AASB 124: the directors, the Company Secretary, the chief financial officer, persons having authority and responsibility for planning, directing and controlling the activities of the Company, and any other person notified by the Board. Subject to Closed and Prohibited Periods, the short-term trading ban, pre- and post-trade notification, the section 9 derivatives criteria and the section 8 margin lending disclosure.

tiers.name: Directors
tiers.description: Directors of WAF, a subset of Key Management Personnel, with the additional Appendix 3X, 3Y and 3Z filing obligation within three business days of appointment, a change of interest or resignation.

tiers.name: Related Persons
tiers.description: Spouses, de facto spouses, parents and children of Applicable Persons, and entities controlled by Applicable Persons. Expressly caught by the short-term trading ban, the exemption process, the margin lending disclosure and the notification rules for Key Management Personnel.

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: WAF may impose additional Prohibited Periods when senior management becomes aware of a matter considered price sensitive, or which the Chairman or the Managing Director deems price sensitive. The policy does not say whether such periods are announced or kept confidential, and sets no limit on their length.

rules.detail: Derivatives as defined in section 761D of the Corporations Act, over shares, performance options or performance rights, are permitted only if all five criteria are met: the securities are fully vested, the maturity date falls outside a Prohibited Period, WAF is not a counterparty, the derivative is used to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of WAF options or to protect the value of the security against tax liabilities, and the transaction complies with all applicable laws. No Board approval is required outside a Prohibited Period, but the section 10 notification rules apply and evidence that the criteria are met must accompany the notification.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel may only enter into transactions involving derivatives (as defined in section 761D of the Corporations Act) (Derivatives) in respect of securities in WAF (including shares, performance options and performance rights) if the following criteria are satisfied

rules.detail: A derivative over securities that are not fully vested, including performance options and performance rights, fails the first criterion and is prohibited outright. There is no Board waiver of the section 9 criteria; the section 7 exemption power is confined to dealing during a Prohibited Period.
rules.evidence: a) the relevant securities are fully vested;

rules.detail: Section 9 binds only Key Management Personnel. Employees, advisers, contractors and consultants who are not KMP are subject to no derivatives criteria, no Closed Periods and no notification, only the insider trading prohibition.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel may only enter into transactions involving derivatives

rules.detail: Products which operate to limit economic risk in WAF holdings are securities for the purposes of the policy, and hedging by derivative is governed by the section 9 criteria. A hedge over fully vested shares is allowed only for the two permitted purposes, must mature outside a Prohibited Period, and must be notified two business days in advance with evidence that the criteria are satisfied.
rules.evidence: securities include shares, options, derivatives and other financial products that can be traded on a financial market including financial products issued or created over WAF securities by third parties and products which operate to limit economic risk in securities holdings in WAF

rules.detail: Hedging of unvested securities, expressly including performance options and performance rights, is prohibited because the section 9 vesting criterion cannot be satisfied.
rules.evidence: a) the relevant securities are fully vested;

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named, but any prepaid forward, collar or similar structure is a Derivative in respect of WAF securities and must satisfy the section 9 purpose test. A structure entered into to raise liquidity, diversify or fund general expenditure serves neither permitted purpose and is therefore prohibited. Only two purposes qualify: protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of WAF options, and protecting the value of the security against tax liabilities.
rules.evidence: d) the Derivative is used for the purposes of protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of options granted by WAF or to protect the value of the security in respect of tax liabilities that may become due and payable;

rules.detail: Short selling is nowhere mentioned. A short position established through a derivative would still have to satisfy the section 9 criteria, and a purchase and sale of the same securities within three months would breach the short-term trading ban.
Securities lending is not named and is not within the definition of dealing, which is limited to applying for, acquiring, disposing of or agreeing to apply for, acquire or sell securities.

CFDs are not named but are derivatives within section 761D of the Corporations Act, so they fall within section 9 and would fail the purpose criterion in 9(d), and a cash-settled CFD would also not be protecting an asset supporting an option exercise loan or a tax liability.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel may only enter into transactions involving derivatives (as defined in section 761D of the Corporations Act) (Derivatives) in respect of securities in WAF

rules.detail: Margin lending over WAF securities is permitted, for KMP and Related Persons, subject to a conduct requirement that the facility terms must not require dealings when the KMP is prohibited from dealing, and to disclosure to the Company Secretary within ten business days of the number of securities, the trigger events for disposal, and the ability to meet a margin call, with an ongoing duty to report changes.
rules.evidence: Within ten business days of a Key Management Personnel or a Related Person entering into a margin lending arrangement involving WAF's securities, the relevant Key Management Personnel must provide the Company Secretary with the following information

rules.detail: Section 8 binds only Key Management Personnel and their Related Persons; margin lending by other employees, advisers, contractors or consultants is unregulated.

Granting an encumbrance over WAF securities is not prohibited and is not a dealing, but the policy expressly contemplates it: the Board may seek information from KMP about encumbrances granted or margin loans taken out over their securities and may require them to keep the Company Secretary informed of changes. Disclosure is on Board demand rather than automatic.
rules.evidence: The Board may seek information from Key Management Personnel about their level of ownership of WAF's securities and about any encumbrances granted or margin loans taken out in respect of those securities.

rules.detail: The conduct requirement is drafted broadly around arranging finance where WAF securities are provided as collateral, not just margin lending, and requires that the obligations do not conflict with the policy, in particular that the terms do not require dealings in WAF securities during a Prohibited Period. There is no prohibition and no approval requirement; the ten business day disclosure obligation is expressed only for margin lending arrangements.
rules.evidence: Key Management Personnel should ensure that when arranging finance either for themselves or through their Related Persons, where WAF securities are provided as collateral, such obligations do not conflict with their obligations under this policy.

rules.detail: A three month holding period test defined as the purchase and sale of the same securities within three months, applying at all times to KMP and their Related Persons. Uniquely, the Board may on application exempt a person from this prohibition in exceptional circumstances.
rules.evidence: Short-term trading is defined as the purchase and sale of the same securities within a three month period. In order to prevent the unfair use of information, Key Management Personnel and their Related Persons are generally prohibited from short-term trading at all times.

financing.price_trigger_guidance: Key Management Personnel should ensure that the terms of any margin lending arrangements do not require dealings in WAF securities at a time when Key Management Personnel are prohibited from dealing in WAF's securities. Trigger events for disposal of the secured securities, and the ability of the person to meet any margin call, must be disclosed to the Company Secretary.

Key Management Personnel; trigger: on Board demand, covering level of ownership, encumbrances granted and margin loans taken out; to the Board and the Company Secretary; deadline: as required by the Board

exemption_authority: The Board only. It may give prior written clearance in exceptional circumstances, such as severe financial hardship or a court order requiring sale, for a member of Key Management Personnel or a Related Person to deal during a Prohibited Period (section 7.1), and may on application exempt them from the short-term trading prohibition in exceptional circumstances (section 5). Clearance is refused if WAF is in possession of Inside Information, and the Board may impose conditions including the effective period. There is no power to waive the section 9 derivatives criteria.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Derivative is used for the purposes of protecting the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of options granted by WAF or to protect the value of the security in respect of tax liabilities that may become due and payable
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This is the decisive clause: a collar is permitted only where it protects collateral for a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of WAF options, or protects against a tax liability, so a funded collar raised for liquidity, diversification or general purposes is prohibited outright, while an option-exercise-funding facility with a protective collar fits the wording precisely.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the Derivative has a maturity date that falls outside a Prohibited Period
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Because Prohibited Periods run for one week before to one business day after every quarterly, half year and annual report, the expiry date of both collar legs must be diarised around a dense quarterly reporting calendar, and any roll or extension must land on a clear date.

bespoke_clauses.clause: WAF is not a counterparty to the Derivative
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: A bank counterparty is expressly contemplated and permitted; only the company itself is excluded.

bespoke_clauses.clause: the relevant securities are fully vested
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Performance options and performance rights cannot be collared until vesting, and there is no Board waiver of this criterion.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel should ensure that when arranging finance either for themselves or through their Related Persons, where WAF securities are provided as collateral, such obligations do not conflict with their obligations under this policy. In particular, Key Management Personnel should ensure that the terms of any margin lending arrangements do not require dealings in WAF securities at a time when Key Management Personnel are prohibited from dealing.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The facility must be drafted so that no mandatory sale, top-up or delivery obligation can be triggered during a Prohibited Period, which constrains margin call mechanics even though section 6(b)(ii) excludes an actual enforcement sale from the policy.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The following dealings ... are excluded from the operation of this policy: ... The disposing of securities ... as a result of a secured lender exercising its right under a margin lending arrangement;
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: An enforcement sale by the lender sits outside the policy entirely, including during a Prohibited Period, which protects the executive if the bank has to realise the collateral.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board may seek information from Key Management Personnel about their level of ownership of WAF's securities and about any encumbrances granted or margin loans taken out in respect of those securities. The Board may also require them to keep the Company Secretary informed of changes to such information.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The security package over the collared shares is disclosable to the Board on demand and, through the continuous disclosure hook, potentially to the market.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Key Management Personnel are required to notify WAF of all intended dealings in WAF's securities ... two business days before such intended dealings.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Outside Prohibited Periods there is no approval gate at all, only a two business day advance notice and a post-trade price confirmation, so execution timing is within the executive's control, but the notice period must be built into pricing.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Board may on application exempt Key Management Personnel or their Related Persons from this prohibition in exceptional circumstances.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Unlike most peer policies the three month holding period ban can be waived by the Board, which gives a route to unwind or restructure a collar inside three months.

summary: A funded collar is possible for WAF Key Management Personnel only in a narrow form. Section 9 permits derivatives over WAF securities without Board approval, and expressly allows a bank counterparty, but only if the securities are fully vested, the derivative matures outside a Prohibited Period, and it is used to protect the value of an asset supporting a loan taken out to fund the exercise price of WAF options or to protect against a tax liability; a collar entered into to raise general liquidity or to diversify fails that purpose test and is prohibited. Where the purpose test is met the structure is otherwise well supported: there is no prohibition on encumbering WAF shares or on secured financing, an enforcement sale by a secured lender is excluded from the policy entirely, and the only gates are a two business day advance notice to the Company Secretary with evidence that the section 9 criteria are satisfied, a post-trade price confirmation within two business days, Appendix 3Y filing for directors, and margin lending disclosure within ten business days. The facility must be drafted so it cannot compel a dealing during a Prohibited Period, which is a real constraint given that Prohibited Periods surround every quarterly, half year and annual report. Tenor should exceed three months to avoid the short-term trading ban, although the Board can exempt that prohibition in exceptional circumstances.
